# NATIVE PLATFORM REFERENCE: DESKTOP (reference/desktop.md)

# Desktop platform

For native desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux: GPUI, Electron, Tauri, Qt, WinUI, AppKit, GTK. When the toolkit is GPUI, [gpui.md](gpui.md) loads alongside this file.

On desktop, the visitor mode narrows what expression may override. Window, input, and menu conventions govern structure in every mode; brand expresses through the layer the OS leaves open (accent, type, iconography, motion, content).

## The desktop slop test

Would someone who lives in desktop software all day trust this app, or feel they are using a website in a frame? The tells: phone-sized padding on a 27-inch screen, actions that only a mouse can reach, no shortcuts, no context menus, a hamburger menu hiding the commands, every error in a toast, one centered column wasting a wide window, custom window chrome that breaks dragging and snapping. Default to what the OS already taught the user; depart only for a reason they would thank you for.

## Window & layout

- **Resizable all the way.** Layouts hold from the minimum window size to an ultrawide monitor. Set a real minimum size; below a width, panes collapse or stack instead of shrinking their text. <!-- rule:desktop-layout-resizable -->
- **Panes, not pages.** Sidebar, content, and inspector side by side, with draggable splitters whose sizes persist between launches. Navigation keeps context visible instead of replacing the whole window. <!-- rule:desktop-layout-panes -->
- **Window chrome keeps its jobs.** A custom title bar still drags the window, double-clicks to maximize (zoom on macOS), and leaves room for the traffic lights on the left (macOS) or the caption buttons on the right (Windows), including Snap Layouts on the maximize button. <!-- rule:desktop-layout-window-chrome -->
- **Pointer density.** A precise pointer allows compact rows (24–32 px) and tight toolbars. Touch-sized padding is a phone habit; use it only when touch screens are a stated target. <!-- rule:desktop-layout-density -->

## Input

- **Keyboard first.** Every action is reachable from the keyboard. Shortcuts follow the OS: Cmd on macOS, Ctrl on Windows and Linux; Cmd/Ctrl+, opens settings, Cmd/Ctrl+W closes the window or tab, Esc dismisses, Cmd+Q quits on macOS. Menus and tooltips show the shortcut next to the command. <!-- rule:desktop-input-keyboard-first -->
- **Visible focus.** Keyboard focus draws a clear ring; Tab order follows reading order; closing a dialog or popover returns focus to what opened it. <!-- rule:desktop-input-focus -->
- **Hover informs, never gates.** Hover states and delayed tooltips are expected on desktop. An action that appears only on hover also needs a keyboard path and a context-menu entry. <!-- rule:desktop-input-hover -->
- **Right-click works.** Objects (rows, files, tabs, selections) have context menus with their actions, mirrored in the menu bar or command surface. <!-- rule:desktop-input-context-menu -->
- **Selection behaves like the OS.** Click selects, Cmd/Ctrl-click toggles, Shift-click extends, arrow keys move, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all. Drag and drop works where objects move. <!-- rule:desktop-input-selection -->

## Menus & commands

- **macOS has a menu bar.** App, File, Edit, View, Window, Help, with the standard items in their usual places. Windows and Linux apps may use an in-window menu or a command surface, but the standard shortcuts still work. <!-- rule:desktop-menus-standard -->
- **A command palette for wide apps.** Apps with many actions get a searchable palette (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P or Cmd/Ctrl+K). It adds discovery; it does not replace menus or shortcuts. <!-- rule:desktop-menus-palette -->
- **Edit commands everywhere.** Undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, and select all work in every text field and on selections. <!-- rule:desktop-menus-edit-commands -->

## Typography

- **System UI faces or one deliberate brand face.** SF Pro on macOS, Segoe UI Variable on Windows, the desktop's UI font on Linux. A brand face carries display moments; a generic default carries nothing. <!-- rule:desktop-typo-faces -->
- **Desktop scale.** Body text sits at 13 px (macOS) to 14 px (Windows); secondary text never goes under 11 px. Respect the OS text-size and display-scale settings. <!-- rule:desktop-typo-scale -->

## Color & appearance

- **Follow the OS appearance.** Light and dark track the system setting by default, with an in-app override. Both appearances are designed, not inverted. <!-- rule:desktop-color-appearance -->
- **One accent, used for state.** Selection, focus, primary actions, and links carry the accent (the system accent or one brand color); large surfaces don't. <!-- rule:desktop-color-accent -->
- **Quiet text still reads.** Meta text, placeholders, and disabled labels keep 4.5:1 against their surface in both appearances; muted is a lightness step, not a fade to nothing. <!-- rule:desktop-color-quiet-text -->
- **Materials come from the platform.** Vibrancy (macOS), Mica and Acrylic (Windows) come from the OS APIs; hand-rolled blur reads as a web port. <!-- rule:desktop-color-materials -->

## Components & feedback

- **Familiar controls.** Checkboxes, radio groups, popup buttons, segmented controls, steppers, sliders, sortable tables, and tree views behave like the OS versions, including their keyboard handling. <!-- rule:desktop-components-familiar -->
- **Modal only to block.** Dialogs are for decisions the app cannot continue without. Button order follows the OS (macOS: primary on the right; Windows: primary first, then Cancel); Enter confirms the default, Esc cancels. <!-- rule:desktop-components-dialogs -->
- **Errors stay near their cause.** Validation errors sit beside the field, failed operations beside the object they failed on. Toasts are for confirmations that need no action; system notifications are for background events while the window is not focused. <!-- rule:desktop-components-feedback -->

## Motion

- **Short and functional.** 100–200 ms transitions for panes, popovers, and state changes; no page-transition theater. Honor Reduce Motion (macOS) and "Animation effects" off (Windows). <!-- rule:desktop-motion-functional -->

## Verifying the build

- **Screenshots come from the app window, never a browser.** macOS: `screencapture -l <window-id> <path>` (or `-w` to pick the window). Windows: capture the window itself (PrintWindow with full-content rendering for GPU-drawn windows). Linux: the compositor's window capture. Capture the minimum window size and a large one, in both appearances. <!-- rule:desktop-verify-window-capture -->
- **Do a keyboard pass.** Walk the main flow with the keyboard only: focus visible, nothing unreachable, shortcuts as listed. <!-- rule:desktop-verify-keyboard-pass -->
- **Check the scale factors.** Look at 100% and 200% display scale; blurry icons, 1 px lines that vanish, and clipped text show up there. <!-- rule:desktop-verify-scale -->
- **Say which OS produced the evidence.** Per-OS conventions (menu bar, chrome, button order) can only be confirmed on that OS. <!-- rule:desktop-verify-os-honesty -->

---

# TOOLKIT REFERENCE: GPUI (reference/gpui.md)

# GPUI toolkit

For desktop apps built with GPUI (Zed's UI framework), including apps on gpui-component. Loads with [desktop.md](desktop.md); the platform conventions there still decide structure, this file says how to express them in GPUI.

## Where design lives in GPUI code

- **Styles are builder methods.** `div().flex().gap_2().px_3().rounded_md().text_sm()` reads like Tailwind: one spacing step is 4 px (`p_2` = 8 px), a rem is 16 px. Keep the steps; reach for `px(..)` only for values the scale cannot express. <!-- rule:gpui-style-scale -->
- **Colors and fonts come from a theme, never from the view.** Put tokens in one place (a `theme` module of zero-argument functions and constants, or a `Global` read through `cx`), and call them from views: `.bg(theme::surface())`, not `.bg(rgb(0x161618))`. An inline `rgb(..)` in a view is a token that escaped. <!-- rule:gpui-theme-tokens -->
- **Appearance switches the tokens, not the views.** Read `window.appearance()` and re-resolve on `cx.observe_window_appearance(..)`; token functions return the light or dark value. Views never branch on dark mode themselves. <!-- rule:gpui-appearance -->
- **Set type once at the root.** Font family, base size, and line height go on the window's root element and inherit; children change only what differs. Dense lists set an explicit `line_height`. <!-- rule:gpui-root-type -->

## Keyboard, focus, and commands

- **Commands are actions.** Declare them with `actions!`, bind them with `KeyBinding::new(..)` under a `key_context(..)`, and handle them with `.on_action(..)`. That makes every command rebindable, menu-able (`cx.set_menus(..)`), and listable in a palette. A click handler alone is a command only the mouse can run. <!-- rule:gpui-actions-keybindings -->
- **Focusable views track a handle.** Interactive regions own a `FocusHandle` and call `.track_focus(&handle)`; give them a visible `.focus(|s| ..)` style. Restore focus to the opener when a popover or modal closes. <!-- rule:gpui-focus -->
- **Icon-only buttons get tooltips.** Every icon-only control sets `.tooltip(..)` with its name and shortcut. <!-- rule:gpui-icon-tooltips -->
- **Stateful interaction needs an id.** `.hover(..)`, `.active(..)`, `.on_click(..)`, and tooltips need `.id(..)` on the element; stable ids keep that state across renders. <!-- rule:gpui-element-ids -->

## Layout and performance

- **Long content is virtualized.** Use `uniform_list` (same-height rows) or `list` for anything that can grow past a screen; a `children(..)` over thousands of items lays all of them out every frame. <!-- rule:gpui-virtualized-lists -->
- **Panes resize, text truncates.** Give flexible children `.flex_1().min_w_0()` so long text truncates or wraps instead of pushing the pane wider; `.overflow_hidden()` on the pane, `.text_ellipsis()` on single-line labels. <!-- rule:gpui-flex-overflow -->
- **Custom title bars keep window behavior.** With `TitlebarOptions { appears_transparent: true, .. }`, leave the drag area free (`window_control_area` on Windows) and position content around `traffic_light_position` on macOS. <!-- rule:gpui-titlebar -->

## Motion

- **Use the shipped easings.** `.with_animation(id, Animation::new(Duration::from_millis(150)).with_easing(ease_out_quint()), |el, t| ..)`. Skip `bounce(..)`; reserve `pulsating_between(..)` for indicators tied to live state. <!-- rule:gpui-motion -->

## What the detector reads

The design hook and `impeccable detect` read GPUI builder chains in `.rs` files and resolve theme functions and constants across the Cargo workspace, both branches of an `if is_dark() { .. } else { .. }` included. They report `overused-font`, `side-tab`, `border-accent-on-rounded`, `low-contrast`, `gray-on-color`, `tiny-text`, `dark-glow`, `ai-color-palette`, `bounce-easing`, `pulsing-dot`, `nested-cards`, and `gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow`. Styles inside closures (`.when(..)`, `.hover(..)`) are conditional and not read, and values that only exist at runtime stay unknown. An empty result is not proof of a clean window: check contrast, overflow, and density on a screenshot.

## Verifying the build

- **Capture the GPUI window itself.** GPUI draws with Metal, DirectX, or Vulkan, so a plain window grab can come back blank. When the app runs a debug build with `impeccable-gpui-probe` attached (`{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui status` answers), capture the set in one call: `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui capture --out .impeccable/review --sizes <min>,<large> --appearances dark,light`. Without the probe: on Windows `PrintWindow` with `PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT`, on macOS `screencapture -l <window-id>`. <!-- rule:gpui-verify-capture -->

## Live variants

With the probe attached, `live` and `generate` run on the window instead of a browser:

1. Ask the user to press `ctrl-alt-i` in the app and click the element (or run `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui pick --x <x> --y <y>` from a capture's coordinates, in logical pixels). `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui selection --wait` returns its source line, style, and bounds.
2. Write 2–4 distinct directions as style patches in the JSON shape the selection printed (`"background": "#rrggbbaa"` is accepted as a solid fill), label each in a few words, and send them: `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui variants --file <json>`. They show at once; nothing rebuilds.
3. The user switches with `ctrl-alt-←/→` and accepts with `ctrl-alt-enter`. `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui decision --wait` returns the accepted patch.
4. Write the accepted patch into the builder chain at the source line, in the app's own vocabulary: scale methods (`.p_3()`), theme tokens for colors, not raw values. Rebuild and capture to confirm.

Patches cover style only. A variant that changes structure, children, or copy is a code edit; with the probe, build it as a slot so the user still compares live:

1. Put the alternatives behind one `match impeccable_gpui_probe::slot("<id>", &["<current>", "<label>", ..], cx) { 0 => current, 1 => .., _ => .. }` in the view's `render`. Arm 0 is the current design. Rebuild once.
2. `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui slots` lists the slots; `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui slot --id <id> --index <n>` shows an arm, for captures or a `snapshot` of each arm.
3. With no style variants shown, `ctrl-alt-←/→` switches the active slot's arms and `ctrl-alt-enter` accepts; `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui decision --wait` returns `{slot, index, label, source}`.
4. Keep the accepted arm's code, delete the `match` and the other arms, and rebuild. Release builds always take arm 0, so never ship a slot. <!-- rule:gpui-live-variants -->

## Window snapshot

When the probe is built with its `snapshot` feature (gpui-pre with the new-horizon-code-repo/gpui patch), `{{scripts_path}}/impeccable gpui snapshot` returns what the window actually painted and checks it: `low-contrast` and `gray-on-color` against the composited fill behind each text, `tiny-text`, `text-overflow` for text cut off by its clip, `overused-font` for the face actually used, and from resolved element styles `side-tab`, `border-accent-on-rounded`, `nested-cards`, `dark-glow`, `gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow`, and `ai-color-palette`, each at the source line of the element. Run it in both appearances (`POST /appearance` through `capture --appearances`, or the app's own switch) and at the smallest supported size; it sees resolved theme branches and `.when(..)` styles that the source scan cannot. A probe without the feature answers 501; fall back to captures. <!-- rule:gpui-snapshot -->

---

DESKTOP_TOOLKIT: gpui. The design hook and `<IMPECCABLE> detect` read GPUI builder code in `.rs` files: source rules only, with colors and fonts resolved from the Cargo workspace's theme functions and constants. They cannot see what the window paints, so verify contrast, overflow and density from a window screenshot. When the app's debug build attaches impeccable-gpui-probe, `impeccable gpui` captures the window and runs live style variants (reference/gpui.md); without it, live mode and `generate` do not apply.
